types.why: a count with a true zero

types.label: Temperature (°C)
types.why: 0 °C is not 'no temperature'; differences are meaningful, ratios are not

types.label: Feels-like temperature (°C)
types.why: same scale as temperature: no absolute zero

types.label: Wind speed (km/h)
types.why: 0 km/h is calm; any value in between is possible

types.label: Season
types.why: named and ordered in time (Winter → Spring → Summer → Fall) but the gaps are not a measured quantity

types.label: Year
types.why: like 'Year enrolled' in class: ordered, equal gaps, but year 0 is only a position on the scale

types.label: Month
types.why: Jan < Feb < … < Dec is an order, not a magnitude

types.label: Holiday
types.why: yes / no label; can only be checked for equality

types.label: Day of week
types.why: named days with an order inside the week

types.label: Weather situation
types.why: clear < mist < light rain: ordered by severity, gaps not measurable

types.label: Day type
types.why: Working day / Weekend / Holiday are names only

types.label: Date
types.why: ordered with equal one-day gaps; no 'zero date'; one value per day

properties.question: Is the information correct in every detail?
properties.check: cnt = casual + registered holds on 731 of 731 days; the counts come from the operator's own trip log, the weather from a public weather service.

properties.question: How comprehensive is the information?
properties.check: 0 missing cells out of 11,696; all 731 calendar days from 2011-01-01 to 2012-12-31 are present.

properties.question: Does it contradict other trusted sources?
properties.check: One value contradicted its neighbours: humidity 1 day at 0 % (2011-03-10, physically impossible). It was replaced in Unit 1 by the mean of the day before and after.

properties.question: Do you really need this information?
properties.check: instant (a row number) and dteday (a text copy of the date) were dropped; the normalised temp/atemp/hum/windspeed columns are kept only through their de-normalised copies.

properties.question: How up-to-date is it, usable for real-time reporting?
properties.check: The data ends on 2012-12-31, about 14 years ago. Good for learning the methods; it would not describe today's bike demand.

classification.geographical: Not applicable: every row is the same city (Washington DC), so there is no area to classify by.

reasons.pair: temperature vs day of the week
reasons.text: the calendar cannot change the weather, so whatever small r appears is chance.
both rise on warm days (r with temperature +0.54 and +0.54); the weather is the third variable behind their correlation.
warm air evaporates more water and moist air changes how fast the ground warms; each affects the other, like price and demand in class.

types.basis: direction in which the variables move
types.example: rentals and temperature move together (r = +0.627, positive); rentals and wind move apart (r = -0.234, negative).
simple: rentals vs temperature alone (r = +0.627); partial: rentals vs humidity with temperature held constant (Unit 4.4); multiple: rentals vs temperature and humidity together (Unit 4.3).

types.basis: constancy of the ratio of change
types.example: rentals vs temperature are roughly linear up to about 25 °C; above that the mean per class stops rising (5,418 then 4,840 rentals), so the ratio of change is not constant at the hot end.
